title: The Met presents 'Tapa: Art of the Gift in Polynesia', exploring historic bark cloths
summary: At the heart of cultural and political diplomacy in the islands of Polynesia are vibrant bark cloth textiles, known as tapa that signify status and play a central role at all major ceremonial events. Known locally as masi, siapo, or hiapo the cloth is produced from the softened inner bark of trees, and is characterized by its unique materiality and the dynamic geometric designs that are painted, stamped, or stenciled onto its surface. Part of a textile tradition developed in the islands of Southeast Asia over 3,500 years ago, the transformation of individual strips of fiber into an entirely new surface evokes the reproductive potential of land (vanua; fanua), encapsulating its abundance and agency. Tapa: Art of the Gift in Polynesia will bring together 13 impressive works from the islands of Fiji, Samoa, Futuna, and Niue, highlighting spectacular, supple, and finely produced examples of bark cloth from The Met collection in addition to sculpted works and an exceptional hiapo on loan fr

title: Stray melodies: A darkly funny dog tale authored and lavishly illustrated by Walton Ford
summary: Exquisitely drawn and joyfully off the leash, Dog Song follows two musical hounds searching for inspiration for their next album, but driven by very different instincts. David is orderly, bookish, contemplative; Jimmy is altogether more appetite-led. David sniffs out bookshops, while Jimmy prowls parks, backstreets, and the shadowy corners of Berlin’s canine underworld. What unfolds is a picaresque tale of misadventure that’s by turns scrappy and sharp. Join their quest for the perfect filing cabinet, a run-in with guards at the Berlin Wall, and some very ill-advised drinking. Authored and exquisitely illustrated by celebrated artist Walton Ford, it takes place in a pre-unification Berlin that’s evoked with operatic flair and cinematic intensity. title: Library of Congress acquires stenographic copy of Theodore Roosevelt's 1912 Milwaukee speech
summary: The Library of Congress has acquired a bound volume containing 15 tipped-in pages of a stenographic version of Theodore Roosevelt's Milwaukee, Wisconsin, speech of Oct. 14, 1912. The pages record the speech Roosevelt delivered from the auditorium stage after receiving a gunshot wound from attempted assassin John Schrank outside the Gilpatrick Hotel. This copy of Elbert Martin's typed stenographic version of Roosevelt's speech contains numerous penciled emendations and alterations to the text made by Roosevelt himself. When Roosevelt made the changes, and for what purpose or publication, are not currently known. (The holes that are visible on the first two pages of the document are unrelated to the assassination attempt and are not bullet holes.) title: Exhibition at the National Gallery explores 19th-century Black portrait studios
summary: Remember Me: Picturing African Americans in Early Photography charts the evolving understanding of portrait photography as a tool of representation among African Americans and illustrates the richness and complexities of Black life and culture in the 19th and early 20th centuries. Featuring some 70 works drawn from the National Gallery’s collection, the exhibition traces African American photographers and portrait subjects in the nascent days of photography’s development, chronicling the evolution of the medium as a means to define Black community, aspiration, and identity. title: Exhibition brings together ancient arts and contemporary works in dialogue with nature
summary: Jeanne Bucher Jaeger presents Garden of love, an exhibition inspired by Guillaume Logé's book of the same title, and curated by its author. For more than a century, the gallery's identity has naturally resonated with this theme, as reflected in its longstanding commitment to artists whose creative practice is guided by universal, social, environmental, and humanistic values. These are artists who work with the forces of nature, weaving together humanity, history, memory, the cycle of the seasons, the immemorial, and the present day. Spanning from ancient arts to contemporary creation, the exhibition brings together works from different periods in a dialogue centered on nature and love. What if love were to reinvent itself by opening up to nature?

title: Zander Galerie presents fifth solo exhibition of architectural photography by Candida Höfer
summary: Zander Galerie opened the exhibition Between by Candida Höfer, one of Germany’s foremost contemporary artists and a leading figure of the Düsseldorf School of Photography. Bringing together colour photographs from 1983 to 2021 that focus on spatial situations of transition, the exhibition has been conceived specifically for the gallery’s spaces in Cologne. Attentive to the inner structures they portray, the works sharpen the viewer’s percep­tion of space and, in turn, heighten awareness of the interior surroundings in which they are shown. This is Höfer’s fifth exhibition with the gallery, following her most recent presentation, Lumière, at Zander Galerie Paris. The title can be read in more than one way, and the exhibition invites visitors to find their own. Those who step into the gallery will discover that Between begins at once, without preamble. title: Marc Brandenburg explores urban reality, social tension, and photographic negatives in solo show at Thaddaeus Ropac
summary: Thaddaeus Ropac Salzburg presents an exhibition by German artist Marc Brandenburg, bringing together several series, including new works created in 2025 for the Berlinische Galerie. The Berlin-based artist is known for his highly detailed pencil drawings, in which he documents everyday urban life whilst subtly alluding to the crises of our time. The silvery, reflective quality of the graphite lends an otherworldly quality to the everyday motifs – like negatives of snapshots from a strange parallel world. His creative process always begins with photographs, which he takes himself during nocturnal city walks or sources from magazines and other media. The inversion of light and dark – a signature technique Brandenburg introduced in the 1990s – continues to characterise his work today. title: Peter Doig and Pierre Soulages lead Ketterer Kunst's December Evening Sale in Munich
summary: A monumental painting by Peter Doig and an important early abstraction by Pierre Soulages will lead Ketterer Kunst's Evening Sale on December 4, 2026, in Munich, bringing together 60 works spanning modern and contemporary art. With estimates reaching €2.5 million, the auction presents an international selection of paintings and works on paper by artists including Marc Chagall, Max Beckmann, Lyonel Feininger, Pablo Picasso, and Alexej von Jawlensky. The sale's highest-valued work is Peter Doig's By a River (2004), an atmospheric oil painting estimated at €1.5 million to €2.5 million ($1.68 million to $2.8 million). Measuring 200 by 186 centimeters, the composition belongs to a significant period in the Scottish-born artist's career, when his experiences in Trinidad became increasingly important to his distinctive approach to figurative painting. title: Rashid Johnson explores fatherhood, identity, and autonomy in new exhibition
summary: Rashid Johnson presents an exhibition of new work that considers the complex relationship between fathers and sons. Including five new mosaic works, a group of suspended sculptural figures known as the "Exhausted Figures" and one new film, "Birthday Boys" (2026), the presentation explores tensions between the fundamental imperatives of intimacy and independence, inheritance and self-determination, considering what it means to recognize another person as separate from oneself, even when that person shares one's history, gestures and features. In the film, Johnson draws on the idea of mirroring to reflect on the shifting relationship between father and son over time, particularly as a child moves into adolescence and increasingly asserts his own identity and prerogatives. title: A Gentil Carioca showcases drawings and paintings by Swiss-based artist Diego Kohli
summary: A Gentil Carioca is presenting Dança para montanhas, by Diego Kohli, marking his first exhibition in Brazil. Through drawings and paintings, hands and feet dance across landscapes where body and world merge, moving between dream and everyday life. Following his first artist residency in Brazil, at Casa VOA, Kohli incorporates Rio de Janeiro’s landscape into a universe of incomplete bodies in constant transformation. Through drawing and painting, the artist explores the relationships between figure and ground, expression and representation, creating scenes in which the familiar becomes strange and the landscape reveals itself as an integral part of the experience of being in the world. Diego Kohli (b. 1991) lives and works between Basel, Switzerland, and Madrid, Spain. title: From Maine to California, Academy Art Museum takes visitors on a journey through American art
summary: The Academy Art Museum presents From Sea to Shining Sea: American Landscape Painting, 1850–1950, a blockbuster exhibition exploring a century of American art through the landscapes that helped shape the nation's cultural identity. On view Nov. 7, 2026, through May 23, 2027, the exhibition brings together nearly 50 paintings from a major American collection, featuring some of the most celebrated artists in American art history. Featuring works by Albert Bierstadt, Childe Hassam, George Inness, Robert Henri, Fitz Henry Lane and N.C. Wyeth, the exhibition showcases artists who helped define how Americans saw and understood their country. From dramatic mountain vistas and rugged coastlines to quiet rural scenes, their paintings captured not only the beauty of the natural world but also the changing identity of a growing nation. Arranged geographically and chronologically, From Sea to Shining Sea takes visitors on a visual road trip

title: CLAMP presents 'Studio Nudes', exploring live models in art from the 1940s to today
summary: CLAMP is presenting “Studio Nudes,” an extensive group exhibition exploring artists' use of live models in their work from the 1940s to the present. Bringing together an array of photography, drawing, and painting, the show investigates how modern and contemporary practitioners challenge, amend, and reframe classical artistic traditions. The history of the studio nude in art spans from ancient academic practices to the current day. In Ancient Greece, the male nude was celebrated through athletics and sculpture, representing civic glory, heroism, and divine perfection. Conversely, during the Middle Ages, nudity was largely restricted and tied to theological concepts of shame, sin, vulnerability, or Last Judgment scenes. The Renaissance revived classical proportions, bringing male and female models back into the studio—though public display of the artworks required mythological, historical, or religious disguises to remain socially acceptable. title: Kunsthalle Osnabrück marks planetarium anniversary with site-specific installation by Andrea Pichl
summary: In her work, Andrea Pichl combines art and research. She explores how spaces and people’s lives influence one another. In her artworks, the artist often focuses on historic buildings and standardised building components. [‘Standardised’ here means: the building components were always the same. They were used in many different buildings.] For Andrea Pichl, they tell the story of the political and economic developments of their time. They bear the traces of history. At the Kunsthalle Osnabrück, Andrea Pichl is presenting an exhibition to mark the 40th anniversary of the planetarium at the Osnabrück Natural History Museum. The planetarium’s dome was built by the civil engineering firm of Ulrich Müther from Rügen in the former GDR, with construction managed by architect Gertrud Schille. title: Ping Zheng explores time, nature, and memory in new series of works on paper at Kristen Lorello
summary: Kristen Lorello is presenting ‘Light Hour,’ Ping Zheng’s seventh solo exhibition at the gallery. New paintings on paper in the artist’s signature medium of oil stick on paper mark an exciting moment in the Chinese-born, New York-based artist’s technical and stylistic development. In her new works that blend naturalism, landscape, and pattern, Zheng delves further into the exploration of landscape as an intensely personal, spiritual space. Ping Zheng’s visions of swirling rivers, reflected pools, and mountains opening to luminous orbs capture, meditate, and transport the viewer. She translates her own free, joyful and tranquil experiences of nature into spiritual propositions that all are invited to share. title: University of Miami School of Architecture to represent the United States at the 2027 Venice Architecture Biennale
summary: The University of Miami School of Architecture (U-SoA) has been selected by the U.S. Department of State to commission, organize, and curate the exhibition of the United States Pavilion at the 2027 Venice Architecture Biennale. Titled Earth Craft, the exhibition explores the relationship between American architecture, the land from which it emerges, and the people who shape it. It traces earthen materials from the ground to the finished building and honors the communities of brickmakers, masons, and earth builders who turned local soil into the foundations of public and private life. title: Design Doha 2026 opens with 20 exhibitions exploring ancestral systems, heritage, and economic futures
summary: Qatar Museums opened Design Doha Biennial 2026, bringing together designers, artisans and creative practitioners from across the Middle East, North Africa and South Asia (MENASA) and beyond to explore how traditional knowledge, craftsmanship and contemporary innovation are shaping the future of design. On view through 31 January 2027, the second edition of the biennial features 20 exhibitions, new commissions, public installations and cultural programmes showcasing the region’s design heritage alongside bold new approaches to materials, making and production. Presented under the curatorial vision Translating Knowledge: From Ancestral Systems to Economic Futures, the 2026 edition highlights how traditional practices continue to inform contemporary design and production. title: MASS MoCA opens largest U.S. exhibition of works by French conceptual artist Laurent Grasso
summary: MASS MoCA presents Metaphysical Maze, the largest exhibition to date in the United States devoted to French conceptual artist Laurent Grasso. Installed in the museum’s iconic Building 5, Metaphysical Maze takes the form of an immersive installation bringing together, for the first time, the artist’s most emblematic films, along with the new film Cosmic Drive, produced during his two-year research residency at the SETI Institute in Mountain View, California. Conceived as a journey, the exhibition immerses visitors in a contemplative state that expands their perception of time. Paintings, sculptures, neons and architectural interventions will be presented alongside the films, forming an environment in which the different elements function as a whole. In Grasso’s universe, lines are blurred and time appears suspended within a carefully

title: Sara Cwynar uses film, collage, and nineteenth-century automata to trace the roots of the AI economy
summary: Elephant, a project by Sara Cwynar, on the occasion of the artist's residency at the American Academy in Berlin. On view will be new videos, photographs and a drawing. Cwynar's films and photographs employ a mix of analogue collage, digital modifications and cinematic techniques to create works with a distinct aesthetic, a dense mix of historical references, found images, and traces of contemporary image worlds. Her process includes photographs that are themselves photographed, arranged in real life with everyday objects, re-photographed and filmed or put into motion. The effect closely resembles a kind of visual free association floating in your head—what thought can feel like. For her presentation at the gallery, she draws on a project concerning automatons. A small elephant from the late 19th century recurs as symbolic presence.

title: parrasch heijnen pairs Amy Lincoln and Craig Kauffman in dual exhibition
summary: parrasch heijnen is presenting Craig Kauffman / Amy Lincoln, an exhibition pairing new paintings by New York–based artist Amy Lincoln (b. 1981, Bloomington, IN) with select historic sculptures by Craig Kauffman (1932, Los Angeles, CA – 2010, Angeles City, Philippines). This exhibition brings together two artists deeply engaged with the experience of light and matter as they unfold within a spatial and temporal environment. Distinct in dimensionality, material, and process, both Kauffman and Lincoln treat surface not only as a vehicle for image-making, but as an active site where color and perception converge. Amy Lincoln applies chromatic pigment in thin, successive layers across carefully ordered divisions of the pictorial plane. title: Major exhibition traces the shared themes and distinct styles of the Wyeth family
summary: The New Britain Museum of American Art presents The Wyeths: Three Generations | Works from the Bank of America Collection from November 20, 2026, through March 21, 2027. The exhibition features remarkable paintings, drawings, and illustrations spanning the early 1900s through the early 2000s, highlighting the Wyeths’ creative legacy and distinct artistic styles. Notably, these generational works invite museumgoers to explore the Wyeth family's creative legacy. For more than a century, the Wyeth family has created art that enraptures the imagination. The Wyeths: Three Generations | Works from the Bank of America Collection presents more than sixty paintings, drawings and illustrations by N. C. Wyeth, his son Andrew and his grandson Jamie, along with works by N. C.’s daughter Henriette and her husband Peter Hurd. The

title: National Museum of Asian art exhibition draws unexpected connections between Chinese textiles and Japanese metalwork
summary: A new exhibition at the Smithsonian’s National Museum of Asian Art brings together late-imperial Chinese textiles and contemporary Japanese metalwork—two different art forms separated by time, material and place—to explore overlooked similarities. Open Saturday, Nov. 7, 2026, through Sunday, Nov. 28, 2027, “Woven and Cast: Chinese Textiles and Japanese Metalwork from the Shirley Z. Johnson Collection,” features the collections of philanthropist Shirley Z. Johnson (1940–2021) that she donated to the museum. When displayed side by side, the textiles and metalworks reveal unexpected commonalities in texture and luminosity that result in striking visual combinations. The exhibition joins

title: National Museum of American History explores the history and disparities of American healthcare
summary: The Smithsonian’s National Museum of American History opened “First Do No Harm,” an exhibition that explores science, medical practice, public health and how practitioners, inventors, patients and communities have shaped healthcare in the United States. Featuring stories about efforts to reduce suffering, extend lives and provide better healthcare for all, the exhibition opened to the public Friday, Nov. 6, and will be on view for about three years. Inspired by the ancient charge to “first, do no harm,” healthcare practitioners have advanced medicine to improve people’s lives and developed cutting-edge technologies that have revolutionized medicine. Not everyone, however, has benefited equally from medical advances, and some innovations have also raised new challenges and consequences. The core of the exhibition looks

title: Museum of Neon Art showcases historic signage, automatic pinsetters, and iconic bowling culture in new exhibition
summary: The Museum of Neon Art invites visitors to step inside their new exhibit “Wonder Lanes: The Signs and Style of Mid Century Bowling,” which explores how Southern California gave birth to a new generation of family-friendly, architecturally striking bowling centers. The exhibition opened to the public November 7, 2026 and includes historic neon, a documentary, and bowling memorabilia. It is being supported by sponsor Lucky Strike Entertainment, one of the world's premier owner-operators of location-based entertainment destinations. Before bowling became a nostalgic pastime, it was one of postwar America’s most spectacular forms of entertainment. In Southern California, bowling centers transformed

title: Marc Straus presents 'Hewn in Blue', ceramic sculptures by Josh Cloud
summary: Marc Straus is presenting Hewn in Blue, an exhibition of new sculptures by Los Angeles-based artist Josh Cloud. The title speaks to the making of a self: who we were, are, or will be, shaped by what happens to us and by our own hand. Cloud builds in ceramic, stacking rounded, organic forms and layering glaze until they read as faces, figures, or something closer to plants and coral. The works are lighthearted, even whimsical, yet they carry material that is not: grief, loss, the weight of history. Floodplain reads as a feline face with pots stacked above it. Some can be read as masks: faces made solid, held between the self and the world.
